name: toast
title: Toast
description: A short message from the application, not from the game: reconnecting, saved, copied. A pill at the top of its container at the floating depth, three seconds, one at a time. A game outcome never uses it; that is `feedback`, which knows how to celebrate and how to be wrong. A toast knows neither and is deliberately quiet: a polite status region a screen reader mentions without interrupting, no focus, no trap, nothing to press. It renders the one message it is given and reports when its time is up; a host with a queue shows the head of it and advances on `onDismiss`. Never fetches, never decides what to say and never remembers what it said.
docs: Put `position: relative` on the surface the toast belongs to and render it inside; it sits centred at the top. Pass `open` and `onDismiss` as a controlled pair: after `duration` milliseconds (three seconds unless told otherwise; `Infinity` waits for the host) it calls `onDismiss`, and the host closes it. Put the words in `children` and, for a saved or copied, a mark from `glyphs` in `glyph`. Show one at a time. Never put a game outcome in it: a correct answer, a score, a reward are `feedback`.
